newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslav, Croatia banks sign cooperation protocol.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslav, Croatia banks sign cooperation protocol.

text.p: Yugoslavia's Komercijalna Banka and Croatia's Promdei Banka signed a protocol on cooperation on Friday in the first inter-bank agreement since the break-up of the former Yugoslav federation in 1991.

"We have set up correspondent relations with Promdei Banka of Zagreb and agreed to open accounts through which we will make payments and give guarantees to business partners in Yugoslavia, Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina," Komercijalna Banka vice president Panta Plazinic told Reuters.

The first agreement between a Yugoslav and Croatian bank since the two countries established diplomatic relations last month will enable non-cash payment operations between the two and Bosnia-Herzegovina.

Promdei Banka, founded in 1990, has branches in the Bosnian cities of Sarajevo and Mostar, while Komercijalna banka emerged from the leading Yugoslav state bank Jugobanka. Both the banks involved in the new deal are private.
"This is the start of Yugoslavia's financial relations with Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina and will enable our businessmen to cooperate with these two republics," Plazinic said.
He said turnover by year-end could reach 50 million German marks ($33 million), but the pace would depend on the banks' clients and their interest in economic cooperation.

The Yugoslav news agency Tanjug quoted Promdei Banka and Promdei Holding president Ibrahim Dedic as saying cooperation was established in record time as the first concrete step in overcoming problems in financial transactions and mutual trade.
Both banks will provide export credits to firms from their territories and enable normal links between the economies of the three states.
"This is just the start. We will see how it goes, but both our customers and those who are not can count on doing business with both Croatia and Bosnia-Herzegovina," Plazinic said.
"We have created the preconditions, but economic interest will decide. Our banks are a guarantee that business will be carried out correctly."
Other forms of inter-bank cooperation were also on the table, such as travellers' checks and servicing of pensions for citizens of former Yugoslav republics once inter-state agreements are reached.
Plazinic said although some payments operations existed during the 3 1/2 year international embargo against rump Yugoslavia, transactions went through Hungary.

Plazinic said the ice was broken with the reopening of the eastern wing of the Adriatic oil pipeline running from Croatia to Serbia, for which the first payment for oil deliveries went through Komercijalna banka.
"Every beginning is difficult, but it is also the first marketing step in the right direction."
